deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Disabling NTP and repeated reboots are state-changing; restore NTP and handle the operator dwell.

cases.purpose: Stress warm reboot recovery 500 times and measure RTC/system time drift after the specified idle period.
cases.execution_boundary: The agent can run read-only baseline/post checks and a controlled reboot loop after approval; the long dwell, recovery supervision, and any physical/AC portion require operator confirmation. NTP must be restored afterward.
required_inputs: Dedicated SUT and 500-reboot approval
Exact standard-time source and idle/dwell duration
Recovery/OOB access and reboot timeout policy
util-linux/systemd tools and NTP restore procedure
cases.evidence_and_risk: Disabling NTP and repeated reboots can disrupt the OS and management access. Capture pre/post lspci, boot/reboot results, RTC/UTC timestamps, timeout/recovery events, and restore NTP after the test.
discussion_needed: Confirm whether the 24-hour idle is required after the 500 reboots and whether any AC-cycle step is actually part of this source row; the source procedure itself says warm reboot only.
cases.independent_conclusion: Reclassify from BLOCKED to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. The procedure and acceptance criteria are identifiable; duration, state change, and recovery require explicit approval.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Test TPM function by vendor tool; collect results/photos and unexpected logs.
source_reread.criteria: Test TPM function by vendor tool.

deepseek_reference_reread.ai_packages_needed: vendor TPM tool (user provides; e.g. tpm2-tools / vendor diagnostic)
deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Exact vendor TPM tool and invocation are not specified; run only after user supplies them.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Vendor tool may perform destructive TPM operations.

cases.purpose: Run the approved vendor TPM diagnostic and verify the TPM function against its vendor-defined criteria.
cases.execution_boundary: The vendor tool, exact invocation, and safety mode are user/vendor prerequisites. The agent can run a confirmed read-only or approved diagnostic and capture output; it must not invent TPM operations.
required_inputs: Exact TPM tool/version and command
Vendor criteria and expected output
TPM state/ownership/lockout pre-check
Confirmation that the tool does not clear or alter TPM state, or an approved recovery plan
cases.evidence_and_risk: TPM commands can alter ownership, keys, NV data, or lockout state. Capture pre/post TPM state and full vendor output; execute only after explicit user confirmation.
discussion_needed: Provide the vendor tool, invocation, and whether the test is read-only or changes TPM state.
cases.independent_conclusion: Reclassify from BLOCKED to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. Missing vendor tool details are an obtainable prerequisite, not a permanent blocker.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Verify that OS installation with the TPM device enabled succeeds; collect results/photos and unexpected logs.
source_reread.criteria: Verify can install OS with TPM device enabled.

deepseek_reference_reread.ai_packages_needed: OS installer media (user provides) + tpm2-tools (post-OS check)
deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Operator-assisted OS install with TPM enabled, followed by /dev/tpm0, TPM dmesg, and systemd-cryptenroll checks.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: OS installation repartitions the disk; use a dedicated user-designated target.

cases.purpose: Install the approved OS with TPM enabled and verify the installed Linux environment detects the TPM device and supports the required TPM function.
cases.execution_boundary: BIOS/installer interaction and target selection are manual/user-confirmed; post-install TPM detection and Linux evidence can be automated.
required_inputs: OS image/media and version
Dedicated installation target and boot mode
TPM BIOS state and required setting
tpm2-tools or approved post-install commands
Backup/recovery and user approval
cases.evidence_and_risk: OS installation can destroy the selected disk and change boot state. Capture target identity, BIOS TPM state, install result, /dev/tpm0, TPM kernel logs, approved TPM command output, and recovery/NTP not applicable.
discussion_needed: Confirm the dedicated installation target and exact TPM success criterion before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: Reclassify from BLOCKED to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. This is the same automation boundary as a user-confirmed OS install with an automatable TPM post-check, independently applied to this row.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Verify SUT status after using SF600 flash successfully; collect results/photos and unexpected logs.
source_reread.criteria: Verify SUT status after using SF600 flash successfully.

deepseek_reference_reread.ai_packages_needed: SF600 ROT flash tool + signed PFR image (user-provided)
deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Vendor SF600 tool performs the ROT/PFR firmware write; agent can collect post-flash dmesg, uptime, and lspci evidence.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Destructive ROT/PFR firmware flash; use approved image and no production execution.

cases.purpose: Flash the approved ROT/PFR firmware with SF600 and verify the SUT returns to a stable, expected state.
cases.execution_boundary: The SF600 firmware write requires vendor tooling, signed image, exact target identity, and explicit approval; post-flash OS/BMC/PCIe health checks can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact ROT/PFR and board identity/current version
Signed target image/hash and compatibility data
SF600 tool/version and approved invocation
Maintenance window, stable power, recovery image/programmer, and rollback ownership
cases.evidence_and_risk: ROT/PFR flashing can brick the platform or change security/boot behavior. Preserve pre-flash firmware/PCIe/BMC/SEL evidence, validate image/signature, and capture flash transcript, post-flash firmware identity, boot/OS/BMC health, and recovery readiness.
discussion_needed: Provide the exact target ROT/PFR image and SF600 procedure plus recovery path before execution. The need for these vendor artifacts is not itself BLOCKED.
cases.independent_conclusion: Reclassify from BLOCKED to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. This is a vendor firmware prerequisite plus automated post-flash verification.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Assert TPM physical presence with an on-board jumper or switch, enter BIOS F1 Security settings, enable secure boot and TPM, change Security Boot mode, save/reboot, and verify the mode changed.
source_reread.criteria: Security mode can be changed successfully.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Read mokutil secure-boot state and ROT/PFR/secure-related dmesg lines over SSH; an operator must assert TPM physical presence and navigate BIOS F1 to change the security mode.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: ROT security-mode change requires a physical TPM-presence assertion and BIOS setup interaction; operator required.

cases.purpose: Change the approved security mode with TPM physical presence asserted, then verify the resulting secure-boot/TPM/ROT state after the BIOS change and reboot.
cases.execution_boundary: The TPM physical-presence jumper or switch and BIOS F1 navigation are manual and require an operator. The agent can perform read-only pre/post state collection and verify the resulting OS-visible security state after the approved change and reboot.
required_inputs: Exact source and destination security modes
Approved TPM physical-presence jumper/switch procedure and reset state
Exact BIOS menu path and secure-boot/TPM dependency
mokutil and approved ROT/PFR state evidence method
Recovery plan if the platform fails to boot or the security mode change is not reversible
cases.evidence_and_risk: A BIOS security-mode change can alter boot policy and prevent the expected OS from starting. Capture the pre-change secure-boot/TPM/ROT state, BIOS screenshots or operator record, reboot/POST result, post-change mokutil output, relevant dmesg/SEL/BMC evidence, and recovery status. Do not clear existing logs merely to create a baseline.
discussion_needed: Confirm the exact source and destination security modes, whether secure boot and TPM must both be enabled for the transition, and the approved recovery path before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: The DeepSeek partial/hybrid assessment is directionally correct. Improve it to explicitly require the target mode, TPM physical-presence and BIOS transition procedure, pre/post state evidence, and recovery planning. The missing parameters are user/vendor prerequisites, not a permanent BLOCKED condition.

source_reread.procedure_summary: The source says to check TPM in BIOS and check the TPM device in the OS, with the stated intent that TPM be disabled; Windows Device Manager and Linux lspci absence are listed as evidence.
source_reread.criteria: TPM can be disabled in BIOS and the device is absent; Windows expects no TPM device in Device Manager, while Linux expects no TPM device in lspci.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: An operator disables TPM in the BIOS Security/TPM page; the agent checks /dev/tpm*, lspci TPM output, and /sys/class/tpm/tpm0 over SSH.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: The BIOS change is manual; the reference does not provide a physical recovery path or distinguish authoritative Linux TPM evidence from lspci output.

cases.purpose: Disable TPM through the approved BIOS setting and verify, on the selected operating system, that no usable TPM device is exposed after reboot.
cases.execution_boundary: The BIOS setting change and reboot are operator-controlled. After the operator confirms the target BIOS setting, the agent can collect Linux device-node/sysfs evidence and approved TPM capability/readiness evidence; Windows Device Manager remains an operator or Windows-agent check. lspci alone is not authoritative for TPM absence.
required_inputs: Exact BIOS menu path and target TPM-disabled state
Selected OS and its authoritative TPM absence check
Dedicated SUT, reboot approval, and recovery path to re-enable TPM
Approved post-reboot commands and expected absence semantics
Preserved pre-change TPM/boot/security evidence
cases.evidence_and_risk: Disabling TPM can affect measured boot, encryption, attestation, and OS security policy. Preserve pre-change state and do not clear logs. Capture BIOS setting evidence, reboot/POST result, Linux /dev/tpm* and /sys/class/tpm evidence or Windows Device Manager evidence, relevant dmesg/SEL/BMC output, and the re-enable/recovery result. Do not use lspci absence alone as proof because TPM is not generally a PCIe device.
discussion_needed: Confirm the exact BIOS TPM control, selected OS, authoritative absence criterion, and whether any disk encryption or measured-boot dependency must be suspended before the change.
cases.independent_conclusion: Change the historical NO/BLOCKED interpretation to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. The manual BIOS operation is identifiable and the OS post-check is automatable, but the source criteria need an OS-specific evidence method and an explicit recovery path. The missing confirmation is a prerequisite, not an irreducible blocker.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Use a vendor tool to test TPM, execute the tool, run its full TPM test menu, retrieve the result, and expect no error with result code 0001FFFF.
source_reread.criteria: The test completes with no error state and result 0001FFFF.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Read-only SSH checks for /dev/tpm0, /dev/tpmrm0, TPM sysfs, and tpm2_getcap; the interactive licensed vendor full-TPM test and 0001FFFF result must be run by an operator.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: The vendor TPM test is interactive and may be licensed or state-changing; the agent cannot drive its menu.

cases.purpose: Run the approved vendor TPM diagnostic in its full-test mode and verify the vendor-defined successful result code 0001FFFF without altering TPM ownership or protected state unexpectedly.
cases.execution_boundary: The vendor tool, license, interactive menu, and final result selection require an operator or supported vendor automation interface. The agent can verify TPM presence before the test, collect the vendor transcript or screenshot supplied by the operator, and run read-only post-test OS/TPM evidence checks.
required_inputs: Exact vendor tool name/version, license, and supported invocation
Tool documentation defining full TPM test and result code 0001FFFF
Confirmation whether the diagnostic writes NV data, changes ownership, or affects lockout state
TPM pre-check and post-check commands
Recovery/abort procedure and operator approval
cases.evidence_and_risk: Do not substitute tpm2-tools presence checks for the vendor diagnostic result. Capture the tool version, selected menu/test, complete result including 0001FFFF, operator screenshot or transcript, pre/post TPM state, and unexpected dmesg/SEL/BMC evidence. A diagnostic that changes TPM state requires backup/ownership and recovery controls.
discussion_needed: Provide the exact vendor tool and confirm the meaning of 0001FFFF and whether the full test is read-only before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: Retain the hybrid/partial conclusion but improve the record with the vendor-tool identity, exact success code, state-change boundary, and evidence requirements. The absent tool and invocation are obtainable prerequisites, not a permanent BLOCKED condition.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Assert TPM physical presence, enter BIOS F1 Security settings, enable secure boot and TPM, change Secure Boot mode, save/reboot, and verify the security mode changed.
source_reread.criteria: Security mode can be changed successfully.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Read mokutil secure-boot state and TPM sysfs presence over SSH; an operator asserts TPM physical presence, navigates BIOS F1, changes the mode, and reboots.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Secure Boot mode change requires TPM physical presence and BIOS setup access; do not auto-run.

cases.purpose: Change the approved Secure Boot/security mode with the required TPM state and verify the new mode after reboot using OS-visible secure-boot and TPM evidence.
cases.execution_boundary: The TPM physical-presence action, BIOS navigation, mode transition, and reboot are manual/operator-controlled. The agent can perform read-only pre/post checks with mokutil and TPM sysfs evidence and collect BMC/SEL/OS recovery evidence.
required_inputs: Exact source and destination Secure Boot/security modes
Approved BIOS menu path and TPM physical-presence procedure
mokutil/tpm2-tools versions and expected state output
Dedicated SUT, reboot approval, and recovery path if boot policy prevents startup
Defined post-change evidence and log-preservation procedure
cases.evidence_and_risk: Changing Secure Boot or TPM policy can prevent the installed OS from booting and can affect measured boot or key use. Capture pre/post mokutil state, TPM presence, BIOS/operator evidence, POST/OS boot result, BMC/SEL and relevant host logs. Do not clear existing logs; do not infer a mode transition from a single command without the target-mode record.
discussion_needed: Confirm the exact source and destination modes, whether Secure Boot Standard Mode is required, and the approved recovery path before the operator changes the BIOS setting.
cases.independent_conclusion: The DeepSeek partial/hybrid conclusion is directionally correct. Improve it with explicit source/destination modes, BIOS/TPM prerequisites, recovery ownership, and pre/post state evidence. The operator step and parameters are execution prerequisites, not an irreducible BLOCKED condition.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Assert TPM physical presence, enable Secure Boot and TPM in BIOS, install Windows Server 2012/R2 with RAID support, install the required drivers, run confirm-SecureBootUEFI, perform UEFI/BMC checks, inspect UEFI/BMC logs, reboot, and verify normal boot.
source_reread.criteria: The SUT installs the OS, DD/FW successfully with Secure Boot enabled; CSM is disabled, Secure Boot is Standard Mode, and the SUT reboots into the OS without warning/error.

deepseek_reference_reread.ai_packages_needed: Windows Server ISO + install media; mokutil (for pre-check)
deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Pre-check Secure Boot/Setup Mode over SSH; an operator performs BIOS/TPM setup, selects the installation target, loads the RAID driver, installs Windows and drivers, and collects confirm-SecureBootUEFI and post-reboot evidence.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: OS installation can wipe the boot disk; use an approved ISO and a user-designated backup/recovery plan.

cases.purpose: Install the approved Windows Server image on a dedicated SUT with TPM and Secure Boot configured, install the approved platform/RAID drivers, verify Secure Boot and UEFI/BMC health, and confirm recovery after reboot.
cases.execution_boundary: BIOS setup, physical TPM presence, installation-media interaction, RAID-driver loading, target selection, and driver installation are operator-controlled or require an approved Windows automation channel. Pre-install state checks and post-install/reboot/UEFI/BMC/SEL evidence can be collected automatically once the user supplies the exact target and image.
required_inputs: Approved Windows Server image/version and installation media
Exact dedicated installation disk/RAID virtual disk identity with backup and recovery plan
CSM-disabled/Secure Boot Standard/TPM BIOS configuration and recovery path
Approved RAID, chipset, NIC, VGA, storage, and PCIe driver/firmware set
Exact UEFI/BMC checks and warning/error acceptance criteria
Maintenance-window and reboot approval
cases.evidence_and_risk: OS installation is destructive to the selected boot target and can change boot policy, storage layout, drivers, and BMC/UEFI behavior. Never infer or choose the target disk. Preserve pre-install storage/boot/BMC evidence; capture installer result, driver status, confirm-SecureBootUEFI output, UEFI/BMC/SEL logs, reboot/POST, and normal OS recovery. The source instruction to clear logs must be replaced by evidence preservation and timestamped collection.
discussion_needed: Confirm the dedicated installation target, exact Windows image, the meaning of 'DD and FW', approved driver/firmware versions, and the required UEFI/BMC post-checks before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: The DeepSeek partial/hybrid conclusion is directionally correct. Improve it with destructive-target identity, exact image/driver inputs, Secure Boot/TPM recovery, and explicit post-install evidence. The OS-install and BIOS steps require confirmation but are not a permanent BLOCKED condition because the purpose and hybrid verification path are identifiable.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Power on the server and visually check whether the motherboard ME LED works normally; collect photos and unexpected logs.
source_reread.criteria: The LED working mode matches the product specification.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Physical/visual observation and photograph of the onboard ME/BMC-related LED; SSH cannot verify the LED state.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Physical visual inspection; human presence at the machine is required.

cases.purpose: Visually verify the specified motherboard ME LED state while the server is powered on.
cases.execution_boundary: A qualified operator must identify the correct ME LED, establish the specified power state, observe its color/blink pattern, and capture the physical evidence. There is no reliable automated substitute for the acceptance criterion; host/BMC logs must not be treated as proof of LED state.
required_inputs: Exact board/LED location and label
Product specification defining the allowed color and blink pattern
Required power/boot state
Operator physical access and timestamped photo/video method
cases.evidence_and_risk: Capture a timestamped photo or video showing the LED and the DUT identity, plus the operator's observed color/blink state and power/boot condition. Preserve existing logs rather than clearing them; logs may be supplemental only. Do not infer the physical LED result from BMC heartbeat or host connectivity.
discussion_needed: Provide the exact ME LED specification and observation state so the operator can distinguish a pass from an unrecognized color or blink pattern.
cases.independent_conclusion: The DeepSeek physical-only conclusion is correct, but the second-review taxonomy maps it to MANUAL ONLY rather than leaving it as an unqualified NO/BLOCKED label. The missing LED specification is an execution input to confirm, not a reason to claim remote automation or a permanent semantic blocker.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Power on the server and visually check whether the FPGA LED works normally; the procedure says to check the LPGA LED and collect photos/logs.
source_reread.criteria: The LED working mode matches the product specification.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Physical/visual observation and photograph of the onboard FPGA-related LED; SSH cannot verify the LED state.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Physical visual inspection; human presence at the machine is required.

cases.purpose: Visually verify the specified FPGA LED state while the server is powered on.
cases.execution_boundary: A qualified operator must identify the FPGA LED, confirm whether the source's LPGA wording is a typo or a distinct LED, establish the required power/boot state, observe the color/blink pattern, and capture physical evidence. No reliable automated substitute exists for the LED criterion.
required_inputs: Exact board/LED label and confirmation of the FPGA versus LPGA wording
Product specification defining the allowed color and blink pattern
Required power/boot state
Operator physical access and timestamped photo/video method
cases.evidence_and_risk: Capture a timestamped photo or video showing the identified FPGA LED and DUT identity, plus the observed state and power/boot condition. Preserve existing logs instead of clearing them; logs are supplemental and cannot prove the physical LED result. Do not assume the LED label from the testcase typo.
discussion_needed: Confirm whether 'LPGA LED' is a typo for the FPGA LED and provide the exact FPGA LED state specification before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: The DeepSeek physical-only conclusion is correct, but the second-review taxonomy maps it to MANUAL ONLY rather than an unqualified NO/BLOCKED label. The LPGA/FPGA naming issue and missing LED specification require confirmation, but they do not create an automatable or permanent semantic blocker.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Trigger a system-level fault such as a fan or power fault and verify that the front error button/indicator lights; collect photos and logs.
source_reread.criteria: The error button should light.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: An operator induces or observes the fan/power fault and visually observes or presses the front error/status indicator; the agent cannot see the panel over SSH.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Fault injection and front-panel visual inspection require human control and safe recovery.

cases.purpose: Verify that the specified front error button/indicator lights when an approved system-level fault is induced.
cases.execution_boundary: An operator must select and safely induce the approved fan or power fault, observe the front-panel indicator, and capture the physical result. The agent may collect supporting BMC/SEL/host evidence afterward, but those logs cannot substitute for the visual acceptance criterion.
required_inputs: Exact front-panel button/indicator identity and expected state
Approved fault stimulus and injection method
Abort threshold, redundancy/power constraints, and recovery procedure
Operator physical access and timestamped photo/video method
Post-fault BMC/SEL/host evidence plan
cases.evidence_and_risk: Fan or power fault injection can interrupt service, overheat hardware, or leave the platform in a degraded state. Capture the fault stimulus, LED/button photo or video, timestamps, BMC/SEL/host evidence, and restored normal state. Do not clear existing logs, and do not induce a generic fault without an approved recovery method.
discussion_needed: Confirm the exact fault type, safe injection method, expected indicator behavior, and recovery sequence before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: The DeepSeek correctly recognized the physical visual boundary, but the second-review taxonomy maps the case to MANUAL ONLY. The generic fan/power fault wording needs an approved stimulus and recovery input; it is not by itself a permanent BLOCKED condition because the test purpose is identifiable.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Disable NTP, align SUT time with a standard, perform 1000 warm reboots, and check the final time accuracy.
source_reread.criteria: NTP is disabled, SUT time is adjusted, and final time accuracy is within 5 seconds.

deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: Trigger one warm reboot over SSH and collect post-boot uptime; the reference does not implement the source's 1000-reboot loop or final time-accuracy measurement.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: Disabling NTP and repeated reboots are state-changing and can interrupt the SUT or management connection.

cases.purpose: Run the approved 1000-cycle warm-reboot test with NTP disabled and measure final clock accuracy against a defined standard while confirming recovery after every cycle.
cases.execution_boundary: The agent can automate the approved reboot loop and read-only time/recovery evidence after explicit approval, but it must not start until the SUT is dedicated, NTP restoration and reboot timeout/recovery are defined, and the reference time source is confirmed.
required_inputs: Dedicated SUT and approval for 1000 reboots
Exact standard time source and clock-difference measurement method
NTP disable/restore commands and service ownership
Reboot timeout, reconnect, failure-abort, and OOB recovery policy
Required sample/evidence format for every cycle or aggregated result
cases.evidence_and_risk: Disabling NTP and performing 1000 reboots can disrupt workloads and leave time synchronization disabled. Capture pre/post NTP state, initial and final reference/SUT times, reboot count, each timeout/failure, boot/uptime evidence, and restored NTP state. The DeepSeek one-reboot command does not satisfy the source's 1000-cycle or 5-second accuracy criteria.
discussion_needed: Confirm the standard time source, whether the 5-second tolerance is measured immediately after the 1000th reboot or after a defined dwell, and the required NTP restoration procedure.
cases.independent_conclusion: Keep the hybrid partial conclusion but improve it materially: the source requires 1000 reboots and a clock-accuracy measurement, while DeepSeek only supplied one reboot and uptime. With the exact time/recovery parameters and approval, the activity is executable; the mismatch is not a permanent BLOCKED condition.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Connect the serial port to a client, use a command to update BIOS to the newest version, restart the SUT, and check the BIOS version.
source_reread.criteria: BIOS updates successfully.

deepseek_reference_reread.ai_packages_needed: BIOS image + serial cable/client (operator); biosupdate tool
deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: An operator physically connects the serial client and runs the BIOS update; the reference does not provide an executable flash command or automated post-flash readback.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: BIOS firmware reflash can brick the platform; use an approved image and do not auto-run.

cases.purpose: Flash the approved BIOS image through the designated serial update path and verify the target BIOS version and platform recovery after restart.
cases.execution_boundary: Serial cable/client setup and any vendor-console interaction require an operator. Once the exact target, vendor tool/flash command, image, and recovery plan are supplied, the agent can perform read-only pre/post identity and version checks where the platform exposes them.
required_inputs: Exact motherboard/SUT identity and current BIOS version
Approved target BIOS version, image hash/signature, compatibility and downgrade/upgrade intent
Vendor biosupdate tool, serial settings, exact flash command and confirmation prompts
Stable power/maintenance window and backup/recovery/reflash path
Post-restart BIOS version and hardware-health evidence method
cases.evidence_and_risk: A BIOS flash can render the SUT unbootable and can change firmware settings. Preserve current version, hardware identity, settings, BMC/SEL and boot evidence; capture the complete flash transcript, target image identity, post-restart BIOS version, POST/OS/BMC health, and recovery readiness. Do not clear logs to create a baseline. Never replace the missing vendor flash command with a guessed generic command.
discussion_needed: Provide the exact BIOS image/tool/flash command, serial parameters, target board identity, and recovery procedure before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: Change the historical NO/BLOCKED interpretation to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. The serial connection is a manual prerequisite and the post-flash verification can be automated or operator-supplied; the missing firmware package and command are vendor inputs, not a permanent BLOCKED condition.

source_reread.procedure_summary: Connect the serial port to a client, use a command to update BMC to the newest version, restart the SUT, and check the version; the source specifically says to check the BIOS version after a BMC update.
source_reread.criteria: BMC updates successfully.

deepseek_reference_reread.ai_packages_needed: BMC image + serial cable/client (operator); bmcupdate tool
deepseek_reference_reread.command_summary: An operator physically connects the serial client and runs the BMC update; the reference does not provide an executable flash command or automated post-flash readback.
deepseek_reference_reread.risk: BMC firmware reflash can interrupt management access or leave the platform unrecoverable; use an approved image and do not auto-run.

cases.purpose: Flash the approved BMC firmware through the designated serial update path and verify the target BMC version, BMC availability, and platform recovery after restart.
cases.execution_boundary: Serial cable/client setup and any vendor-console interaction require an operator. Once the exact BMC target, vendor tool/flash command, image, and recovery plan are supplied, the agent can perform read-only BMC version, connectivity, SEL, and host-health checks. The post-update check must verify BMC firmware, not BIOS firmware.
required_inputs: Exact BMC/controller and board identity with current version
Approved target BMC image, hash/signature, compatibility and upgrade/downgrade intent
Vendor bmcupdate tool, serial settings, exact flash command and confirmation prompts
Stable power/maintenance window and BMC recovery/reflash path
Post-update BMC version, connectivity, SEL, and host-health evidence method
cases.evidence_and_risk: A BMC flash can interrupt OOB management, reset sensors, affect host service, or require recovery programming. Preserve current BMC/BIOS/SEL and connectivity evidence; capture the complete flash transcript, target image identity, post-update BMC version, reconnect result, SEL/health state, and host recovery. Do not clear logs and do not substitute the source's BIOS-version check for BMC-version evidence.
discussion_needed: Provide the exact BMC image/tool/flash command, serial parameters, target controller identity, expected BMC downtime, and recovery procedure before execution.
cases.independent_conclusion: Change the historical NO/BLOCKED interpretation to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. The serial connection is a manual prerequisite, while BMC post-flash verification is automatable or operator-supplied. The source's BIOS-version readback is a concrete mismatch that must be corrected; missing vendor artifacts remain prerequisites, not a permanent BLOCKED condition.
